subject: CHEMISTRY
pageTitle: Stoichiometry: Mole Ratios and Mass-to-Mass Steps
description: Convert between grams and moles and use the mole ratio from a balanced equation, with two worked chemistry examples.
caption: Stoichiometry in 7 swipes: the grams to moles to moles to grams road map and two worked examples. Save this for your chemistry test. Free Chemistry study guide at precisstudy.com/chemistry (no sign-up).

slides.title: GRAMS TO GRAMS IN THREE STEPS
THE ROAD MAP
lines: grams A → moles A (divide by molar mass)
moles A → moles B (mole ratio from the equation)
moles B → grams B (multiply by molar mass)
slides.note: The balanced equation gives the mole ratio.

slides.title: EXAMPLE 1
slides.problem: N₂ + 3H₂ → 2NH₃. How many moles of NH₃ form from 6.0 mol H₂?
steps: Mole ratio: 2 mol NH₃ per 3 mol H₂

slides.title: EXAMPLE 2
slides.problem: How many grams of NH₃ form from 28 g of N₂? (N₂ = 28 g/mol, NH₃ = 17.03 g/mol)
steps: Mole ratio: 1 mol N₂ makes 2 mol NH₃

slides.title: WATCH OUT
slides.wrong: Use the mass ratio from the equation
points: Coefficients are mole ratios, not mass ratios.
Balance the equation before you start.
Always convert grams to moles first.
